memory_update.text: MIDD should be retained as the main public reference name for commercial kitchen, beverage, refrigeration, soft-serve, IoT/control, and service-density exposure in restaurant equipment.

FARM is a below-300M speculative exception worth tracking only if current filings confirm equipment service, beverage program outsourcing, and customer retention are material enough to offset balance-sheet and micro-cap risk.

HSHCY/Hoshizaki is an underfollowed OTC ADR candidate for the ice/refrigeration sub-node; diligence should focus on US foodservice revenue, service network, approved-vendor relationships, and ADR liquidity.

The strongest chokepoint framing for this node is not generic equipment replacement; it is certified equipment plus field service density, parts uptime, energy/regulatory compliance, and chain-approved standardization across franchise systems.

Need a follow-up search for privately held but influential vendors such as Bunn, Duke, Wasserstrom, WebstaurantStore, and Ali/Welbilt to map public substitutes, acquirers, distributors, or component suppliers.

node: Labor-saving kitchen equipment, beverage equipment, and service networks
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the restaurant equipment/service chokepoint found a concentrated set of public-market exposures around certified commercial kitchen equipment, beverage/coffee equipment service, ice/refrigeration, and aftermarket/service density. The strongest direct public exposures are Middleby and ITW as reference equipment platforms; the more underfollowed/speculative exposures are Farmer Bros. for beverage program plus equipment placement/service and Hoshizaki via OTC ADR for ice/refrigeration equipment used in foodservice. Key unresolved diligence item: verify named QSR/fast-casual approved-vendor status, customer concentration, service revenue mix, parts availability, and whether equipment refresh cycles are accelerating due to labor, energy, menu complexity, or franchise remodel mandates.
